assumptions.statement: The environment is AWS, where Elastic Load Balancers (ELBs) are available and sufficient to handle instance autoscaling, making dedicated load balancer tiers less useful.
assumptions.quote: In the Amazon world these are less useful as we also have ELBs in place to handle the autoscaling of instances.

assumptions.statement: The application servers (frontend/backend hosts) can be made directly available via external ELBs while maintaining security through security group restrictions.
assumptions.quote: add external ELBs to a number of other autoscaling groups (such as the frontend / backend hosts themselves) to make them directly available, but security group restricted.

assumptions.statement: The application servers are capable of handling load balancer processing tasks, such as generating trace IDs, that were previously performed by the dedicated load balancer tier.
assumptions.quote: Some of the LBs processing, such as trace ids, will be pushed down the stack to the application servers themselves.
